why: All three legs check out, and the consequence was measured, not inferred. (1) DOC: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary.md line 231 (the whole '### Project trust' paragraph) carries the quoted sentence VERBATIM: 'Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch.' The rest of the line does not reverse it — it adds 'Trust gates auto-installation of marketplace plugins and execution of project-defined hooks' and that config files take effect, which reinforces what a persisted home grant would unlock. (2) CODE: the cited lines say what was claimed. project-trust-store.ts:114-128 resolve() returns the persisted record for any identity whose persistence is 'stable'; :135-158 record() writes it to CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json for 'stable' and keeps only 'process-only' in memory; project-identity.ts:116-133 sets persistence='process-only' ONLY when statIdentity() fails or reports inode 0. grep -rain 'homedir|process.env.HOME' over packages/shared/src/projects and packages/shared/src/capabilities returns nothing, and the same grep over the layers above (packages/server-core/src, apps/electron/src/main) finds home only in credential-deny-roots, path expansion and getHomeDir — never in the trust path. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and with a positive control. Probe against the real home directory: resolveProjectIdentity(homedir()) -> persistence 'stable', key p_d70d9d9d…; ProjectTrustStore.record(home,'trusted') writes the record to disk; a FRESH store instance (restart simulation) resolves it back as {state:'trusted', persistence:'stable'}. Positive control on the same rig: a process-only identity recorded 'trusted' resolves to {state:'none'} from a fresh instance — the session-only machinery exists and works, home simply never reaches it. One layer up: ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory (the sole raw-path ingress, project-handle-service.ts:140-156, 250-278) ACCEPTS $HOME — isManagedPath rejects only CONFIG_DIR (~/.nessy-agent) and managed workspace roots, and I ran it: validateProjectDirectory('ws-1', homedir()) issued a handle with trustState 'unknown'. The RPC SET_TRUST handler (server-core/src/handlers/rpc/projects.ts:78-85) and the renderer ProjectTrustDialog reach setProjectTrust with no home special case. One layer down: the grant is material — capabilities/resolver.ts:1623-1636 and :1709-1727 withhold project-scope instructions, hooks, MCP and LSP unless trustState==='trusted', so a persisted home grant permanently unlocks execution of anything under the home tree. Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 lists nine and none concerns project trust or the home directory (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows). Not a rename/gateway/subscription product difference either. Caveat recorded rather than used as a refutation: this fork has no CLI 'launch in cwd' — a project root is an explicit folder pick bound to a workspace/session — so 'the prompt reappears on each launch' maps here to 'the grant must not survive a restart', which is exactly what fails.
correctedState: CONFIRMED. The fork treats the user's home directory as an ordinary project root and persists trust for it. ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory accepts $HOME (isManagedPath rejects only CONFIG_DIR and managed workspace roots — project-handle-service.ts:250-278); resolveProjectIdentity($HOME) returns persistence 'stable' because the platform can stat it (project-identity.ts:116-133); ProjectTrustStore.record then writes the grant to CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json and a fresh store instance resolves it as 'trusted' after restart (project-trust-store.ts:135-158, :114-128) — measured directly on this host. Claude Code holds home trust for the current session only and re-prompts each launch. The session-only path exists in our store but is reachable only through a stat failure or a zero inode ('process-only'), never through a home-directory carve-out. Consequence is real, not cosmetic: capabilities/resolver.ts:1623-1636 / :1709-1727 gate project-scope instructions, hooks, MCP and LSP on trustState==='trusted', so one accidental 'Trust' on $HOME permanently enables project-defined hook execution across the whole home tree with no re-prompt. Fix shape: force persistence to 'process-only' (or refuse the grant outright) when the canonical project root equals the home directory, in resolveProjectIdentity or at the ProjectHandleService boundary.
